title: Cipher and Witness
premise: Kestrel Marchetti, an insurance investigator whose photographic memory has quietly unraveled three deaths the police called accidents, is stunned when a drowned man surfaces wearing clothes stolen from their own closet. The victim is Detective Elias Voss, the officer who closed the case of Kestrel's mother's hit-and-run fifteen years ago, and the staged clothing is a message: someone wants Kestrel framed — or warned. As Kestrel digs into Voss's final weeks, they discover he was investigating his own department, and that the hit-and-run was no accident at all but the first move in a cover-up reaching into city hall. With a corrupt captain closing in and their found family — diner owner Marisol and retired archivist Ben — caught in the fallout, Kestrel must decide whether loyalty to the people who sheltered them matters more than the truth they've spent a lifetime chasing. In the end, Kestrel uses their perfect memory to expose the killer in a public records hearing, clearing their name, avenging their mother, and choosing to keep the found family that chose them back.
about_author: T. M. Crane is the pen name of a former forensic claims adjuster who spent a decade reading the small lies people tell on paperwork. They write mysteries about ordinary observers who notice too much, and live in a coastal town they refuse to name.

chapters.title: The Wrong Clothes
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. When a drowned man is pulled from the harbor wearing Kestrel's own jacket and scarf, police treat Kestrel as suspect, not witness. Kestrel's memory reconstructs the theft from their apartment — and identifies the drowned man as Elias Voss, the detective who closed their mother's case. Emotional beat: dread hardening into resolve as Kestrel realizes this is personal.

chapters.title: What Voss Kept
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, with a Marisol interlude. Following Voss's trail, Kestrel finds a hidden notebook in a storage locker: the detective had been investigating his own precinct, and the fifteen-year-old hit-and-run was staged by Captain Rourke to bury an embezzlement scheme. Marisol and Ben insist on helping despite the danger. Emotional beat: the warmth of found family sharpened by the fear of losing them.

chapters.title: Loyalty Has a Price
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Rourke strikes back: Ben is arrested on planted charges and Marisol's diner is burned as a warning, while an anonymous tip frames Kestrel for Voss's murder. Cornered, Kestrel realizes the only surviving evidence is in Voss's notebook — and that Rourke knows it exists, setting a trap at the records archive. Emotional beat: grief and fury fusing into a willingness to risk everything.

chapters.title: Every Detail, Remembered
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. At a public oversight hearing, Kestrel walks the room through fifteen years of details — timestamps, tire marks, the exact wording of Voss's closed-case report — reconstructing the cover-up from memory alone as Rourke watches his story collapse. Ben is freed, Marisol rebuilds, and Kestrel, finally at peace with their mother's truth, chooses the family that stayed. Emotional beat: catharsis and belonging.
